Quick triage notes (pre-bridge):
- Traces show sustained GPU scheduling backlog on the reserved pool nodes; avg GPU utilization is not pegged at 100% but queue length and scheduling latency jumped, indicating head-of-line blocking on large context requests.
- We see a pattern of long sequences (~16k tokens) and a handful of heavy reranking jobs originating from a legacy job queue that started a few minutes before the customer tickets. Those jobs are consuming continuous KV cache entries and causing eviction churn.
- No OOMs or kernel crashes. Not due to model swap.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (can be done now):
1) Activate burst-capacity policy for ReserveX reserved pool (adds two ephemeral GPUs for 30m) — requires ops approval.
2) Apply temporary priority QoS: throttle known low-priority reranking job route and set strict max-context-size for that route.
3) Enable KV cache pinning for ReserveX's route (prevents eviction during this burst window).
4) If (1)-(3) not possible quickly, enable a read-only fallback routing to a compatible, lighter-weight model (rdx-encode-3b) for non-critical traffic.

I attached a quick mitigation script (quick_patch.sh) that stages items 1–3 for ops to execute.

— Marcus Lin
Staff Engineer, Inference Runtime

Subject: Stabilization steps taken and next actions (ReserveX)

Aisha / Jacob — thanks for your patience on the bridge. Short summary of actions we executed and next steps: 

What we did (completed within 35 minutes of first report):
- Activated burst-capacity: 2 ephemeral GPUs added to reserved pool (30m window) — immediate reduction in queueing observed.
- Applied priority QoS: reranking and legacy-job route throttled to 10% of prior concurrency.
- Enabled KV cache pinning on ReserveX route; eviction churn stopped.
- Applied temporary read-fallback for non-critical endpoints to rdx-encode-3b for heavy-context requests.

Impact observed: p95 dropped from 2.2s -> 190ms for reserved generation route; error rate fell from ~6% -> 0.4% over 20 minutes. Throughput returned to ~95% of reserved commit for core route.

Follow-ups and requests:
- We uploaded a detailed mitigation plan and timeline: mitigation_plan_0822.pdf (shared to your Drive link).
- Ops will run a controlled soak test tomorrow 09:00 PT to validate the legacy job backfill pattern that surfaced the contention.
- Post-mortem will be shared within 72 hours. We will include a proposed permanent change set: prioritized KV pinning for top-tier reserved routes, stricter guardrails on cross-tenant long-sequence jobs, and an automatic burst policy for customers above threshold.

If ReserveX wants a temporary account credit while we complete the PM and corrective work, mark here and we'll route to Billing. Vivek asked for a 1-hr recoverability window; we met that threshold.

Thank you — will keep this thread open for any follow-up.

— Sergio
Senior Director, Customer Success (Escalations)
Redwood Inference
